title: Walk both books in order and reconcile project checkpoints
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
After `java-6-05` failed during learning, the user requested an ordered walk through both books and fixes for bugs found. A new book-wide harness runs authored steps from both books in order through the compiled CLI, retaining workspace state between steps. It reports each step, stops a book after its first failure while continuing the other, compares full-walk progress and the CLI version with expected values, and attempts representative Pygame and JavaFX window smoke launches. External projects use headless replay; its harness-only `--relax-output` skips stdout/stderr matching while still checking exit and timeout expectations. The reusable workflow runs on PRs and main pushes and gates tag releases, uploading the JSON report.

Project-root scaffolds now reconcile previous generated-file records before writing the next checkpoint: obsolete unchanged files are removed, missing records forgotten, and modified generated files cause a conflict before removal. Files without generated-file ownership records are excluded from automatic reconciliation; existing overwrite and explicit cleanup rules still apply. The Java content update also adds explicit cleanup for `ThermostatApp.java` at `java-6-05`. Replay reports command details on mismatches and restricts its simple remove shortcut to a single path; native learning displays execution failure details. The content dependency is pinned to a commit and the embedded content updated.

The added tests cover checkpoint reconciliation, replay behavior, failure presentation and workflow wiring. No completed full book-walk result is captured in the available evidence. `bun run check` failed: content sync and typecheck passed, but `bun test` reported 551 passes, 37 skips and 11 failures, including nine five-second timeouts and failures in Maven installation plan and OpenTUI cases. The content pin uses a commit SHA, while the README describes updating a dependency tag; whether that is an accepted exception is unresolved.

For review, start with `scripts/walk-books.ts` and the reusable workflow, then `prepareExerciseFiles` in `src/commands/run.ts` and its checkpoint tests. The replay and learning changes cover the execution and failure paths used by the walk.

title: Test every authored book step in order
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
A failure in Java exercise 6-05 prompted a request to automate walking both books in order, so this adds a compiled-CLI campaign that keeps a workspace per book and exercises authored steps in sequence.

The harness accepts `--binary` (defaulting to the target binary or `bin/aifirst`), `--report` (defaulting to `test-results/book-walk/report.json`), `--book`, `--from`, `--skip-smoke`, and `--keep-workspace`; it reports step and smoke totals and exits nonzero on failure. After a step fails, later steps in that book are marked not-run; graphical smokes launch `py-9-01` and `java-11-01`, alongside replay-based checks, and the reusable Ubuntu workflow installs the book runtimes, builds the binary, runs the walk under Xvfb, and uploads the report even when a step fails. CI calls this workflow for pull requests and main, and release waits for it before the release job.

Previously exercise preparation did not reconcile the recorded files under a shared project root. Preparation now reconciles managed project files against the desired scaffold, removing obsolete files when their generated content still matches and preserving changed files; the store enumerates valid records under a project and can forget a supplied path. Replay can relax captured output for the book walk while checking an expected exit code when specified, and the CLI restricts that option to the book-walk environment; replay output includes timeout status when a command does not match expectations. Portable removal handles multiple paths, and native learning displays command details when execution fails. The Java 6-05 content adds a cleanup rule for `ThermostatApp.java`, the Docker test target installs GTK, and book-walk reports are ignored; the embedded pack version moves from 2.0.0 to 2.0.1 and the generated lockfile is updated.

Tests cover workflow gating and report configuration, restricted relaxed replay, generated-file ownership, failure details, replay matching and removal, and checkpoint transitions including modified files.

The recorded runs were on Linux, so they do not show the Windows-specific paths in the harness or generated-file store running. The session logs contain no run of the changed CI workflows or CI results for the final head.

title: fix: make Claude integration independent of CLI PATH
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Claude Code on Windows can fail its prompt hook and exercise commands when its shell cannot find `aifirst` on PATH. This change installs a Claude-owned Bash launcher pointing to the current CLI and uses it throughout the Claude integration.

On non-Windows platforms path normalization leaves the normalized path unchanged.

Claude skill installation writes the launcher and uses its command in the generated skill, slash commands and replay hook. It recognizes the legacy hook and marked managed hooks for replacement. Permission installation replaces legacy bare-command entries with launcher-based entries while retaining unrelated permissions; permission checks and book mode use the launcher entries, and revocation removes both forms. Existing installations can receive these changes by reinstalling the Claude skill.

The shared instructions now select the PowerShell installer for native Windows and the shell installer for macOS, Linux or WSL, and advise restarting Claude Code and its host after installation. The replay guide documents the launcher, skill refresh migration and platform-specific installers. `test/agents.test.ts` covers path conversion, quoting, launcher forwarding and target-specific instructions; `test/permissions.test.ts` covers migration and revocation of legacy entries. `test/upgrade.test.ts` checks the installed launcher can report the current version with a PATH that cannot resolve `aifirst` when Bash is available.

title: Add Claude Showtail end-to-end scenario harness
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Add a capture and replay harness for three Claude Code scenarios: a multi-prompt train simulator, a sandwich planner with custom answers, and a habit tracker that moves from auto mode into planning. The capture command saves authoring logs, Showtail reports, plans and source checkpoints, generates book content through the sibling content repository, and compares canonical author and learner events and per-turn source files. Raw terminal logs are retained for review; the automated event comparison normalizes volatile output rather than comparing raw terminal bytes.

The fixture tests compare saved author and learner events. Live replay is opt-in with `AIFIRST_CLAUDE_E2E=1`, requires Claude and sibling fixtures, checks the captured Claude version, and verifies each source checkpoint and scenario commands. Capture refuses to overwrite an existing fixture without `--replace`; it records and tolerates the specific known Showtail raw-event verification failure.

Planning replay also retains trailing pre-plan text when entering a workflow without pre-plan operations. title: Fix PR targeting and guard test processes against hangs
body:

Repository resolution uses GitHub's default when it matches a clone remote and uses the default when no origin exists, and otherwise falls back to origin; offline resolution uses origin when available. GitHub operations use the resolved repository when known; doctor and the render preview report the target, and automatic comic attachment checks that target’s visibility. title: Improve judge recovery and comparison reporting
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Judge timeouts can interrupt comparisons, while incomplete usage accounting and duplicate judgment records can distort reports. This change retries recoverable judge failures and improves the accounting and evidence presented in comparison scores.

Previously, judge retries were limited to transient failures; timeouts now share the three-attempt retry budget with backoff, including when a persisted timeout is resumed, and Codex judge timeouts are identified explicitly.

Judge identity is recorded on unsuccessful attempts, and score reports include a judge reliability table alongside writer reliability when judge failures are recorded.

Previously, saved isolation proofs compared the bare model with the arm specification, which could reject effort arms on resume.

Isolation probes now record the full arm specification, while saved proofs using the bare model remain compatible on resume.

Codex runs use rollout usage for main and spawned threads when its input total is at least the stdout total, deduplicating replayed responses by ID; otherwise they retain main-thread usage when available. The artifact records the usage scope when available and the subagent count with all-thread usage. Artifact validation accepts the two usage scopes and checks that the optional subagent count is nonnegative. For older runs, scoring can recover usage from the accepted attempt's saved traces and labels what the cost covers and reports subagents per draft. The judgment walk skips attempt directories containing copies of accepted judgments, and paired scores include per-case deltas against the same-model baseline and a leave-one-case-out range when available.

Writer environment hashes exclude shell and session bookkeeping for Codex and Claude; experiments with a matching legacy hash retain it. This makes comparisons less sensitive to incidental shell state while preserving compatible frozen experiments. 

The changed comparison tests use a fake comparison setup, so they exercise the surrounding code rather than the real setup.

`tests/claude-comparison.test.ts` covers effort-arm proof resume; `tests/codex-usage.test.ts` covers thread usage and trace recovery; `tests/comparison.test.ts` and `tests/recovery.test.ts` cover timeout retries and recovery; and `tests/environment-hash.test.ts` covers environment hash compatibility.

title: Score drafts and report writer reliability across comparison arms

Writers that time out, produce no draft, or fail the scope audit can be retried up to three attempts, and the reliability table reports these failures by arm. A scope-rejected draft is not scored or cached, allowing a fresh sample in a fresh sandbox on retry. A missing PR is classified as `no-draft`, and failure records name the arm. When failures are present, comparison summaries and the score command’s Markdown output include a reliability table with separate no-draft, scope-rejected, timed-out and other failure counts. title: Fix PR targeting and bound stalled test processes
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
PR publishing needs a consistent repository target, including when a branch is pushed from a fork, while Windows CI has encountered test processes that remain running for hours. This change aligns target selection across the workflow and bounds test processes so a stalled run can report a result.

The target is gh's default repository when it matches a clone remote or origin is unavailable; otherwise it is origin. Offline resolution uses origin when available. Context records the target, render binds it to the approval and preview, and publish refuses a changed target when the approval contains a repository. PR and repository metadata calls use the resolved repository when known, and when origin is a fork, PR creation names the fork owner and existing-PR lookup filters by head owner. Check receipts are included even without task bookkeeping, and summary extraction favors wrapper totals on stdout over child output on stderr.

Previously the file runner waited for the child to close without a limit. It now applies a configurable file timeout and, after a completed summary, a grace period before stopping a child and using the summary's failure and error counts; the CI job also has a 45-minute limit. The CLI flushes output before explicitly exiting and can record its exit code for the test guard, which handles a process that remains alive after recording it. The tests also bound CLI calls and redirect their output to files. Target and flow tests use fakes or stubs for collaborators, so they exercise the surrounding logic rather than real GitHub operations.

PR truth resolves the target for existing PR lookup; flow and target tests cover repository selection and refusal after a target change.

The runner passes a per-test timeout, destroys and unreferences a killed child's pipes, and flushes output before the source and packaged runners exit. The CLI clears the exit-file variable from its environment before writing the code, and the test helper routes CLI spawns through the guard. Receipt environment identity ignores terminal and temporary-directory variables while retaining PATH and toolchain identity. The merged-list test accommodates reviewer completion order, and the build identity is updated.

The default file timeout is 15 minutes and the post-summary grace period is 20 seconds; both can be configured. Doctor reports the target and push destination, and the preview notes when the branch is pushed elsewhere. The session's recorded CI results refer to an earlier commit.

title: Fix AIM user serial port detection and writes
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
VEX AIM serial connections need their user port identified so console traffic reaches the intended interface. Previously, location-based classification used the Brain interface layout, and a dedicated user-port write could return after a partial write without flushing.

The commit describes AIM as a composite device with a camera on interfaces 2 and 3, and reports that interface 4 was previously dropped, leaving user traffic to fall back to the system port. For an AIM device, interface 4 is classified as the user port; interface 0 remains the system port, while the existing Brain layout uses interfaces 0 and 2. If location-based classification recognizes no ports, it returns `None` so name-based fallback can run. The tests cover those AIM and Brain layouts and the unrecognized-port fallback, with a helper that adds one to the interface number on macOS. The test comment explains that serialport reports the CDC data interface there as the communication interface plus one.

When a dedicated user port is available, `write_user` now writes the whole buffer, flushes it, and returns its length; errors propagate to the caller. This lets callers rely on a successful return for the complete buffer on that path.

title: Judge drafts across comparison runs
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Comparing composite scores from separate runs leaves uncertainty about how drafts from different writer models fare against each other. This adds `crossjudge` to pair saved candidate drafts from one comparison with baseline drafts from another, without running writers again.

Previously, the CLI set a nonzero exit code when a comparison had pending work. Each input must have one writer model, and the runs must agree on their judge contract, judges, rubric, replicates, split and cases; the current harness must match the contract and rubric too. Drafts and receipts are checked before judge calls, so a missing or invalid draft stops the comparison up front.

Each pair is judged in both orders by the configured judges and uses compare's consensus rule. The output includes consensus and per-judge tallies, per-draft composite and error summaries, and recorded judge costs, writing provenance, pairs and summary JSON files alongside a Markdown summary. This lets a caller compare saved drafts across runs while refusing incompatible inputs. The crossjudge tests cover pairing, consensus and rejection of mismatched runs and missing drafts; they use fake judges rather than real judge providers.

title: Add showtail upgrade for standalone installations
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Adds `showtail upgrade` so standalone installations can update without rerunning the installer. The CLI previously had no self-upgrade command; the existing upgrade module only offered a history migration.

The command checks the latest GitHub release and leaves current or newer installations unchanged. For a newer release, it downloads the platform binary and bundled VSIX, checks the binary's reported version, and replaces both files with rollback on replacement failure. title: Add an in-place update command
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Tracetoon needs an update command so installed users can upgrade without running the installer again. Previously the Windows installer raised an error if it could not find a release.

`tracetoon update` looks up published releases and selects the latest channel by default; `--channel stable` excludes prereleases, while `--to <version>` selects a published version and permits a rollback. `--check` reports availability without installing, and `--exit-code` returns 10 when a newer release is available in check mode. Updates can be disabled with the disable-updates environment setting.

For an eligible installer-managed runtime, the updater verifies downloaded checksums and the skill and runtime build identities before staging the binary, assets and installed skills. It attempts to restore replacements on failures before backups are discarded; hook registration and receipt writing follow that cleanup. If hook registration fails, the command reports how to install hooks manually. Copies managed through `TRACETOON_BIN`, a plugin or bundle, or a different binary are directed to their appropriate update path.

Release selection skips drafts and invalid versions, chooses the newest publication time with version ordering to break ties, and accepts a test server through a configurable update URL. title: Fix AIM user serial port detection and writes
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
AIM devices need their user serial port recognized so that console traffic can use the correct connection. Previously, location-based detection used the Brain interface layout, and a user-port write made one `write` call that could accept part of the buffer.

The AIM commit describes interfaces 2 and 3 as a UVC camera and identifies 0 and 4 as its serial interfaces. The commit reports that interface 4 was previously dropped, leaving the user port absent and causing reads and writes to use the system-port fallback.

For the AIM USB PID, interface 4 is now classified as the user port; the existing interface 0 system and interface 2 user mapping continues to handle the Brain layout. If location detection recognizes no ports, it returns `None` so the name-based fallbacks can run. The location tests assert that AIM interfaces 0 and 4 and Brain interfaces 0 and 2 map to system and user ports respectively, and that interface 9 yields `None`. Their helper adjusts reported interface numbers on macOS; its comment explains that serialport reports the CDC data interface one above the communication interface, which the detection code compensates for.

When a user port is present, `write_user` now writes the entire buffer, flushes it, and returns its length; callers can therefore rely on a successful return representing the complete buffer, matching the system-port send path. body:

For full Windows desktop launches on Wayland, prefer an SDL FreeRDP client when no command is configured. Previously automatic selection used xfreerdp. title: Use SDL FreeRDP for the full desktop on Wayland
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Use the SDL FreeRDP client for the full Windows desktop on Wayland, while keeping the change small enough for upstream review.

Previously, automatic selection looked for `xfreerdp` and the FreeRDP Flatpak.

When no command is configured and the requested mode is `windows` on Wayland, `waGetFreeRDPCommand` now prefers `sdl-freerdp3`, `sdl3-freerdp`, and `sdl-freerdp` in that order, followed by the FreeRDP Flatpak's SDL command.

If none is selected, the existing xfreerdp selection remains available; RemoteApp and other app launches continue down that existing path.

The Flatpak SDL command is also accepted as a FreeRDP command, and the mode argument is passed to the selection function.
